cards.explanation: The answer is Jerusalem, friends! The text says Hezekiah reigns there twenty-nine years (2 Kings 18:2). Home base settled. I once lost my own bakery's front door, and I'm not even moving, so I'm in no place to judge.

The answer is True, friends! The text says, "And he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father David had done." Think about that for a second. A whole kingdom to run, and what the writer wants us to know first is that he did right in God's eyes.

The answer is that he cuts them down, friends! The text says he "…cut down the Asherah poles." That's three jobs in a row: removing, shattering, cutting. It's like someone who wipes the counter, then the floor, then the oven door too.

The answer is False, friends! There's no safekeeping here. The text says Hezekiah "…demolished the bronze snake called Nehushtan that Moses had made…" Moses, Israel's leader, made it back in the wilderness (Numbers 21:9), and still it came down in Hezekiah's day.

The answer is that people had been burning incense to it, friends. The text gives the reason: "…for up to that time the Israelites had burned incense to it." The snake itself came from Moses, Israel's leader, but the people were burning incense to it, so Hezekiah demolished it. Worth noticing that even something with that kind of history didn't get a pass.

The answer is True, friends! The text says, "No king of Judah was like him, either before him or after him." Before AND after. That's a long line of kings, and the writer says none of them were like Hezekiah. Right before that line, the text says he trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel.

The answer is False, friends! The text says, "He remained faithful to the LORD and did not turn from following Him…" No part-time following here. It also says he kept the commandments the LORD had given Moses, Israel's leader.

The word is serve, friends! The text says Hezekiah "…rebelled against the king of Assyria and refused to serve him." That's the king of a powerful empire, and Hezekiah says no. And that same verse says the LORD was with Hezekiah.

The answer is the Philistines, friends! The text says, "He defeated the Philistines as far as Gaza and its borders, from watchtower to fortified city." Watchtower to fortified city. That's a whole stretch of land, not just one corner. Prospering wherever he went, exactly like verse 7 says.
The word is years, friends. The text says, "And at the end of three years, the Assyrians captured it." Three years of siege. That's a long time, and I think it's a heavy part of the story.

The answer is False, friends. The text says, "The king of Assyria exiled the Israelites to Assyria and settled them in Halah, in Gozan by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes." Egypt isn't named here.

The answer is that they would not listen to the LORD or obey, friends. The text gives the reason: "This happened because they did not listen to the voice of the LORD their God, but violated His covenant…" It adds that they "…would neither listen nor obey." I think this one hurts, and it's good the writer says plainly why.
